evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones were different from the ones found in the CXR clones.
source: All of these mutations were different from the ones found in the CXR clones, which suggests that, despite both acting through TOP2A, CX-54161 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently
evidence: This is a primary finding from comparing the mutations in CXR and F14R clones.

claim: CX-5461 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently.
source: All of these mutations were different from the ones found in the CXR clones, which suggests that, despite both acting through TOP2A, CX-54161 and F14512 affect TOP2A activity differently
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that different mutations confer resistance to the two drugs.

claim: All F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461.
source: Strikingly, cell survival assays clearly demonstrated that all of the F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461 (Figure 2D), while showing no resistance to nocodazole (Supplementary file 1), with IC50 values for CX-5461 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1), supporting the concept that the TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones also conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: F14R cells showed no resistance to nocodazole.
source: Strikingly, cell survival assays clearly demonstrated that all of the F14R cells were cross-resistant to CX-5461 (Figure 2D), while showing no resistance to nocodazole (Supplementary file 1), with IC50 values for CX-5461 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells (Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1), supporting the concept that the TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones also conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Supplementary file 1.

claim: F14R cells have IC50 values for CX-5461 that are 3.6- to 16.8-fold higher than the IC50 value of CX-5461 in WT cells.

evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: TOP2A mutations found in F14R clones conferred resistance to the G4 ligand CX-5461.

evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate as compared to WT cells.
source: Importantly, population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations and flow cytometry analyses of 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation in CXR #A6 and F14R #C1 cells revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate of TOP2A mutated clones as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: Flow cytometry analyses of EdU incorporation in CXR #A6 and F14R #C1 cells revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate as compared to WT cells.
source: Importantly, population doubling time determination of five clones carrying different TOP2A mutations and flow cytometry analyses of 5-ethynyl-2′-deoxyuridine (EdU) incorporation in CXR #A6 and F14R #C1 cells revealed no significant differences in the proliferation rate of TOP2A mutated clones as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: The survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin was not significantly different.
source: In addition, the survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin, a DNA TOP1 poison, or calicheamicin, a radio-mimetic compound, was not significantly different.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to calicheamicin was not significantly different.
source: In addition, the survival of WT and TOP2A mutated clones to camptothecin, a DNA TOP1 poison, or calicheamicin, a radio-mimetic compound, was not significantly different.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Camptothecin induces toxic replication-associated DSBs, which are mainly repaired by HR.
source: Since camptothecin induces toxic replication-associated DSBs, which are mainly repaired by HR, while calicheamicin induces DSB in all cell cycle phases, which are repaired by both NHEJ and HR (Elmroth et al., 2003; Furuta et al., 2003), these results indicate that DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Calicheamicin induces DSB in all cell cycle phases, which are repaired by both NHEJ and HR.
source: Since camptothecin induces toxic replication-associated DSBs, which are mainly repaired by HR, while calicheamicin induces DSB in all cell cycle phases, which are repaired by both NHEJ and HR (Elmroth et al., 2003; Furuta et al., 2003), these results indicate that DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells.
source: Since camptothecin induces toxic replication-associated DSBs, which are mainly repaired by HR, while calicheamicin induces DSB in all cell cycle phases, which are repaired by both NHEJ and HR (Elmroth et al., 2003; Furuta et al., 2003), these results indicate that DSB repair mechanisms are proficient in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is inferred from the similar survival of WT and TOP2A mutated cells to camptothecin and calicheamicin.

claim: The sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells.
source: Supporting this conclusion, the sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and the kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and mutant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and TOP2A mutant cells.
source: Supporting this conclusion, the sensitization to calicheamicin induced by an inhibitor of the NHEJ factor DNA-PK was similar in WT and TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and the kinetics of DSB repair after X-ray irradiation measured by flow cytometry analysis of the γH2AX signal were identical between WT and mutant cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: TOP1 levels were unaffected in TOP2A mutated cells.
source: Finally, western blot analysis showed that TOP1 levels were unaffected in TOP2A mutated cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: The resistance to CX-5461 observed in CXR and F14R cells is not associated with major changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that the resistance to CX-5461 observed in CXR and F14R cells is not associated with major changes in proliferation or DNA repair mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: All CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS with IC50 values for PDS 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than the IC50 value of PDS on WT cells.
source: Cell survival assays showed that all CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS (IC50 values for PDS 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than the IC50 value of PDS on WT cells) but with lower resistance indexes than those observed for CX-5461 and F14512 (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1.

claim: CXR clones showed lower resistance indexes to PDS than those observed for CX-5461 and F14512.
source: Cell survival assays showed that all CXR clones were cross-resistant to PDS (IC50 values for PDS 2.7- to 4.4-fold higher than the IC50 value of PDS on WT cells) but with lower resistance indexes than those observed for CX-5461 and F14512 (Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and Supplementary file 1.

claim: All F14R clones were resistant to PDS.
source: More remarkably, cross-resistance studies established that all F14R clones were also resistant to PDS (Figure 2F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The role of TOP2A in the cytotoxicity of CX-5461 and PDS was further supported by the marked resistance to both CX-5461, PDS, and ETP conferred by small-interfering RNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A in HAP1 cells.
source: The role of TOP2A in the cytotoxicity of CX-5461 and PDS was further supported by the marked resistance to both CX-5461, PDS, and ETP (as a control) conferred by small-interfering RNA-mediated depletion of TOP2A in HAP1 cells, with IC50 values similar to those observed for mutant cells (Figure 2G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Stabilization of G4 by ligands provokes cell growth modifications relying on DNA and RNA transaction alterations in cells.
source: In cells, stabilization of G4 by ligands has been shown to provoke cell growth modifications relying on DNA and RNA transaction alterations (Varshney et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: RHPS4 affects both telomere maintenance and mitochondrial DNA replication.
source: The acridine derivative RHPS4, a potent G4 ligand, affects both telomere maintenance and mitochondrial DNA replication (Falabella et al., 2019; Salvati et al., 2007), while two selective bisquinolinium G4 ligands, 360A and PhenDC3, impact on telomeres, gene expression, and RNA metabolism (Dumas et al., 2021; Halder et al., 2012; Pennarun et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 360A and PhenDC3 impact on telomeres, gene expression, and RNA metabolism.
source: The acridine derivative RHPS4, a potent G4 ligand, affects both telomere maintenance and mitochondrial DNA replication (Falabella et al., 2019; Salvati et al., 2007), while two selective bisquinolinium G4 ligands, 360A and PhenDC3, impact on telomeres, gene expression, and RNA metabolism (Dumas et al., 2021; Halder et al., 2012; Pennarun et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: TOP2A mutant cells do not have significantly different modifications in response to RHPS4 and PhenDC3 as compared to WT cells.
source: Through performing cell viability with RPHPS4 and PhenDC3, we revealed that the TOP2A mutant cells do not have significantly different modifications in response to these two chemically unrelated ligands as compared to WT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2G.

claim: TOP2A is specifically involved in the cytotoxic effect induced by the two G4 stabilizers CX-5461 and PDS.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A is specifically involved in the cytotoxic effect induced by the two G4 stabilizers CX-5461 and PDS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: Short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid production of the DSB markers γH2AX and 53BP1 foci in human cells.
source: In human cells, short treatments with PDS or CX-5461 induce rapid production of the DSB markers γH2AX and 53BP1 foci (Rodriguez et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2017; Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations and confirmed by experimental data shown in Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441.
source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: A substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway.
source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is inferred from the increased γH2AX foci production when NHEJ is inhibited, supported by experimental data.

claim: NHEJ is the major DSB repair pathway in human cells.
source: G4-dependent γH2AX foci production is increased in cells incubated with the DNA-PK inhibitor NU7441 (DNA-PKi; Figure 3—figure supplement 2B), indicating that a substantial number of G4-induced DNA breaks are repaired through the DNA-PK-dependent NHEJ pathway, the major DSB repair pathway in human cells (Pannunzio et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In CXR cells carrying different mutations in the TOP2A protein, γH2AX production was significantly reduced as compared to control cells.
source: First, in CXR cells carrying different mutations in the TOP2A protein, clones CXR #A1 (F85I), #A2 (S654N), and #A6 (intron retention), γH2AX production was significantly reduced as compared to control cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands.
source: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands, thereby demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: TOP2 catalytic activity plays a major role in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
source: Pre-incubation with BNS-22 significantly decreased the number of γH2AX foci in cells treated with both G4 ligands, thereby demonstrating the major role of TOP2 catalytic activity in the production of DNA breaks following G4 ligand treatments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental finding that BNS-22 (a TOP2 catalytic inhibitor) reduces γH2AX foci.

claim: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment.
source: Immunofluorescence studies showed that in TOP2A-depleted cells γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: In TOP2A-depleted cells, γH2AX production was strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment.
source: Immunofluorescence studies showed that in TOP2A-depleted cells γH2AX production was abolished upon PDS treatment and strongly reduced upon CX-5461 treatment (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment.
source: In contrast, TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment, while it reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: TOP2B depletion reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
source: In contrast, TOP2B depletion did not impact γH2AX production upon PDS treatment, while it reduced γH2AX production upon CX-5461 treatment to a similar extent to that induced by TOP2A depletion.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Simultaneous siRNA-mediated knock-down of TOP2A and TOP2B further decreased γH2AX production by CX-5461 when compared to the effect of separate siRNAs.
source: Moreover, simultaneous siRNA-mediated knock-down of TOP2A and TOP2B further decreased γH2AX production by CX-5461 when compared to the effect of separate siRNAs (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on the ligand class.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: TOP2B variably contributes to DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands depending on the ligand class.
source: Altogether, these results indicate that TOP2A activity is the main effector of DSBs by clastogenic G4 ligands in human cells, with TOP2B variably contributing depending on the ligand class.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: ETP provoked a strong increase in TOP2A signal that correlated with a similar increase in γH2AX foci.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, B, ETP provoked a strong increase in TOP2A signal that correlated with a similar increase in γH2AX foci (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: A significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals was observed in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS.
source: Using the same approach, we observed a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B), supporting the idea that these G4 ligands mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
source: Using the same approach, we observed a significant increase of TOP2Acc and γH2AX signals in cells treated with CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A, B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, B), supporting the idea that these G4 ligands mediate their cytotoxic effect through stabilizing TOP2Acc.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental finding of increased TOP2Acc signals.

claim: 360A is a bisquinolinium compound that is a potent and selective G4 binder.
source: The bisquinolinium compound 360A is a potent and selective G4 binder that exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells as compared to CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge and confirmed by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 360A exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells as compared to CX-5461 and PDS.
source: The bisquinolinium compound 360A is a potent and selective G4 binder that exhibits a lack of clastogenic activity in most human cells as compared to CX-5461 and PDS (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands.
source: As shown in Figure 4B (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: 360A pre-treatment did not impact on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
source: As shown in Figure 4B (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), 360A pre-treatment strongly reduced the induction of TOP2Acc by both clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the TOP2Acc signal induced by ETP.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands.
source: As expected, inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 360A pre-treatment did not impact on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells.
source: As expected, inhibition by 360A pre-treatment of TOP2Acc formation resulted in a significant reduction in the γHA2X signal induced by clastogenic G4 ligands, without impacting on the formation of DSBs in ETP-treated cells (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing with TOP2Acc.
source: As shown in Figure 4C (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C ), CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing (Figure 4D) with TOP2Acc and induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C, Figure 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
source: As shown in Figure 4C (and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C ), CX-5461 and PDS treatments induced a significant increase in the percentage of BG4 signals colocalizing (Figure 4D) with TOP2Acc and induced a significant increase in the percentage of TOP2Acc signals colocalizing with G4 structures.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Analysis of BG4 signals showed a strong increase of G4 structures in all the treated conditions.
source: Furthermore, analysis of BG4 signals showed a strong increase of G4 structures in all the treated conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The increase in TOP2Acc-G4 colocalizations was not observed in ETP-treated cells.
source: It is noteworthy that the increase in TOP2Acc-G4 colocalizations was not observed in ETP-treated cells, showing that the percentage of colocalization does not result from a global increase of TOP2Acc or BG4 signals induced by the different treatments (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The increased BG4 signal observed in ETP-treated cells probably results from a global increase of DNA supercoiling by ETP, which would promote G4 formation.
source: The increased BG4 signal observed in ETP-treated cells probably results from a global increase of DNA supercoiling by ETP, which would promote G4 formation as shown in several other studies (Sekibo and Fox, 2017; Sun, 2010; Sun and Hurley, 2009).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
source: Altogether, our data support the conclusion that TOP2-dependent DSBs induced by CX-5461 and PDS are associated with G4 structures in cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental findings in the manuscript.

claim: PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases.
source: We observed that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, indicating that PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and a citation to previous literature.

claim: PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent.
source: We observed that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases, indicating that PDS-induced DNA damage is not strictly S-phase dependent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that PDS-induced DSB markers appeared in all cell cycle phases.

claim: DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 also occurs outside of S phase.
source: Using the DNA-base analog EdU to visualize DNA synthesis, we confirmed that DNA damage induction by PDS and CX-5461 also occurs outside of S phase (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A; Rodriguez et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: DNA replication-independent processes are very efficient for the production of DSBs by PDS.
source: Furthermore, comparison of the number of G4 ligand-induced γH2AX foci in EdU-negative cells and in the total cell population indicated that DNA replication-independent processes were very efficient for the production of DSBs by PDS (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of γH2AX foci in EdU-negative cells and total cell population.

claim: DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by DRB.
source: Accordingly, DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by 5,6-dichloro-1-b-D-ribofuranosylbenzimidazole (DRB), an inhibitor of critical phosphorylations in the RNA-Pol-II C-terminal domain (Yankulov et al., 1995; Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: DRB is an inhibitor of critical phosphorylations in the RNA-Pol-II C-terminal domain.
source: Accordingly, DSB production by PDS in HeLa cells was strongly reduced upon inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription by 5,6-dichloro-1-b-D-ribofuranosylbenzimidazole (DRB), an inhibitor of critical phosphorylations in the RNA-Pol-II C-terminal domain (Yankulov et al., 1995; Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription did not impede the accumulation of G4 structures caused by PDS treatment.
source: Importantly, immunofluorescence analysis with the G4-specific antibody BG4 showed that inhibition of RNA-Pol II-dependent transcription did not impede the accumulation of G4 structures caused by PDS treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DRB treatment completely abrogates DSB formation induced by PDS.
source: In this study, we show that DRB treatment, which specifically blocks RNA-Pol II transcriptional elongation, completely abrogates DSB formation induced by PDS and significantly reduces DNA break production induced by CX-5461.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: DRB treatment significantly reduces DNA break production induced by CX-5461.
source: In this study, we show that DRB treatment, which specifically blocks RNA-Pol II transcriptional elongation, completely abrogates DSB formation induced by PDS and significantly reduces DNA break production induced by CX-5461.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: DNA breaks induced by CX-5461 are strongly reduced when both RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I activities are inhibited.
source: Interestingly, we found that DNA breaks induced by CX-5461 are strongly reduced when both RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I activities are inhibited, indicating an important contribution of rDNA transcription in the cellular response to this ligand.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2D.

claim: rDNA transcription has an important contribution in the cellular response to CX-5461.
source: Interestingly, we found that DNA breaks induced by CX-5461 are strongly reduced when both RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I activities are inhibited, indicating an important contribution of rDNA transcription in the cellular response to this ligand.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental finding that inhibiting both RNA-Pol II and RNA-Pol I reduces DNA breaks induced by CX-5461.

claim: Active transcription of rDNA repeats enhances the sensitivity of cells to CX-5461 and DNA damage production.
source: Consistent with our results, active transcription of rDNA repeats has been found to enhance the sensitivity of cells to CX-5461 and DNA damage production (Son et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Topological stresses induced by transcription are mainly resolved by the TOP1 protein in cells.
source: In cells, topological stresses induced by transcription are mainly resolved by the TOP1 protein (Kim and Jinks-Robertson, 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: TOP1 protein plays a major role in countering DNA break formation by CX-5461 and PDS.
source: Here, we show evidence for a major role of the TOP1 protein in countering DNA break formation by CX-5461 and PDS.
